To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the reliability of the solder joints depends on the microstructure and morphology, and that the solder joint microstructure and morphology depend on the interplay of materials and processes.
the reliability of Pb-free solder joints in the electronic package-to-board interconnections can be significantly improved by appropriate selection of the surface materials and soldering processes.

the microstructure and morphology evolution of Pb-free solder joint is a key factor that impacts solder joint reliability, and that the microstructure evolution can be controlled to some extent by the choice of the materials (pad surface finish and solder alloy) and/or by the soldering process (soldering profile).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reliability of Pb-free electronic packages and the solder joint microstructure, which is the most important aspect of the reliability of electronic packages.
the effects of microstructure and morphology on the reliability of solder joint interconnections in electronic packages.
the effects of the microstructure and morphology on joint reliability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the reliability of the solder joints in the package-to-board level interconnection is strongly dependent on microstructure of the solder joint, which is in turn controlled by materials and soldering process parameters.

solder joint reliability is a complex issue that depends on the interplay of several parameters, such as solder composition, solder joint geometry, soldering process, and the environment to which it is exposed.
the solder joint reliability is a function of the solder microstructure, which is determined by the soldering materials, process, and the environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reliability of the electronic assemblies depends strongly on the solder joint metallurgy, which can be controlled by the selection and optimization of materials and processes.
the microstructure and morphology change of solder joint is the key to understand the reliability of the solder joint.
the microstructure of the solder joint is a key factor for the reliability of the interconnections.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reliability of the solder joints is strongly dependent on the microstructure, morphology, and chemistry of the intermetalics formed at the solder/substrate interfaces, and the solder bulk.
the reliability of the solder joint is not only dependent on the microstructure and morphology but also the interaction of the materials and the process.
the reliability of solder joint can be predicted and improved by optimizing the microstructure of solder joints.
